role_name: Enterprise Sales Manager – Agentic AI Solutions
role_description: Owns full-cycle enterprise pursuit and closure of Agentic AI solutions. Bengaluru, work-from-office.
paper_title: Candidate Screening Form – Enterprise Sales Manager, Agentic AI Solutions
paper_notes: Transcribed verbatim from Enterprise_Sales_Manager_Candidate_Screening_Form.docx. All questions are free-text. Marks are not used - this is a screening form, reviewed by a human, not a scored test.

questions.question_text: Where are you based these days?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational. Note whether the location is compatible with daily attendance at the Bengaluru office, and flag any relocation requirement.

questions.question_text: This role is based in Bengaluru and is a work-from-office (WFO) position. Are you comfortable with this, and would you be able to work from our Bengaluru office on a daily basis?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Screening gate. Look for an unambiguous yes. Treat a clear no, or a hybrid-only expectation, as a knock-out for this role and flag it regardless of the rest of the form.

questions.question_text: What is your educational background? If you don't have a CS / engineering degree, how have you built your technical depth?
questions.evaluation_criteria: A CS or engineering degree is not mandatory for this role. Where it is absent, look for a credible substitute: certifications, self-study, time spent with technical products, or the ability to hold a technical conversation evidenced elsewhere in the form (see questions 8 and 10).

questions.question_text: How many years of full-cycle enterprise sales experience do you have selling complex technology to mid to large enterprises?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for full-cycle ownership (prospect to close), not just one stage. Check the figure is consistent with the deal stories given later. Enterprise and mid-market experience counts; pure SMB or channel-only experience is weaker for this role.

questions.question_text: How would you define your current role, and how do you see yourself fitting into this Enterprise Sales Manager position at Valamm.AI?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Two parts, both needed: an accurate description of what they do today, and a considered link to this role showing they have read what it involves. Credit realistic self-assessment including gaps. Deduct for generic ambition statements that would fit any advert.

questions.question_text: Did you carry a quota? What were your targets over the last two years, how did you perform against them, and what was your largest deal size?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for real figures: quota value, attainment percentage per year, and largest single deal. Credit candidates who know their own numbers without prompting and whose figures are consistent across two years. Treat 'always exceeded target' with no numbers as a weak answer.

questions.question_text: How do you build your own pipeline when no leads are handed to you? Describe your prospecting and qualification approach with a real example.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests whether they can self-source. Look for a repeatable method: how accounts are chosen, the research and trigger used, channels and cadence, and an explicit qualification bar. The example should be specific and recent. Deduct where pipeline has only ever arrived from marketing or inbound.

questions.question_text: In simple words, what is an agentic AI solution? Give one example of where it adds value in an enterprise workflow, and one task it should not be trusted to run on its own.
questions.instructions: Please answer in plain, simple language and avoid jargon or buzzwords.
questions.evaluation_criteria: The key technical-comprehension question. A good answer conveys that an agent plans multi-step work, uses tools or systems, and acts toward a goal within guardrails - distinct from a chatbot or a fixed rules engine. The value example should be a concrete workflow. The 'should not be trusted' half matters most: it shows they understand autonomy risk and human-in-the-loop, which is what security and IT buyers will probe. Deduct for buzzword definitions or for claiming an agent can be trusted with anything.

questions.question_text: What AWS or Azure exposure do you have?
questions.instructions: For example: a certification (current or lapsed), working with AWS / Microsoft partner companies, or hands-on / self-learning.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Nice to have rather than essential. Credit any genuine exposure - certification (even lapsed), co-selling with a cloud partner, marketplace experience, or self-directed hands-on learning. An honest 'limited, but here is what I have done' is better than an overstated claim.

questions.question_text: A customer's IT or security team asks how an AI product will fit their existing systems, where their data will sit, and what access controls apply. How would you handle this conversation?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests behaviour in the conversation that most often stalls AI deals. Look for: treating the questions as legitimate rather than rebutting them, separating integration from data residency from access control, naming concrete mitigations (least privilege, human approval, audit logging, private or in-tenant deployment, no-training-on-customer-data, DPA, SOC 2), bringing in a solutions architect or security lead rather than bluffing, and converting security into a stakeholder. Deduct for dismissing the concern, over-promising, or answering only with reassurance.

questions.question_text: Walk us through one enterprise deal you closed – from first contact to close. Who was on the buying committee (business, IT, security, procurement), and who really made the decision?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for genuine multi-threading: several named stakeholder types, who championed it, who could block it, and a clear identification of the economic buyer as distinct from the loudest voice. Credit specifics on commercials, procurement and security review, and on how the deal was actually driven to signature. Deduct for a single-threaded story or one where the candidate cannot say who decided.

questions.question_text: Have you sold AI products or software into enterprises? Which industries do you know best?
questions.instructions: For example: BFSI, Manufacturing, Healthcare, Retail, IT, Education.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for concrete AI or software products sold, the buyer personas reached, and named industries with real depth rather than a list of every vertical. Sector knowledge relevant to our target market is a plus; honesty about where their depth genuinely lies is worth more than breadth claimed without evidence.

questions.question_text: Tell me about a recent deal you lost, and why.
questions.instructions: For example: lost to a competitor, pricing challenge, budget freeze, stuck in security review, or something else.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests candour and diagnosis. Look for a real, recent loss owned without deflection, an honest root cause, and a specific change made afterwards. Deduct for blaming product, pricing or the prospect entirely, for a trivial example, or for claiming no recent losses.

questions.question_text: What is your current notice period, and what are your current and expected CTC (fixed + variable)?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational, for offer planning. Look for a clear notice period and both CTC figures with a fixed/variable split. Do not judge the candidate on the amounts; note only whether the expectation sits inside the approved band.
